claims.statement: EIOPA reported that 50% of non-life insurers and 24% of life insurers were already using AI across areas including fraud detection and claims management, while generative AI expands possible uses and governance challenges.

EIOPA's insurance AI opinion emphasizes risk-based governance and risk management, while the EU AI framework identifies documentation, traceability, accuracy, robustness, transparency, and human oversight as important controls for relevant systems.
Hypothesis: Polish insurers and their AI vendors will pay for a shared but independent domain benchmark when it shortens procurement evidence work and catches regressions before customer exposure.

contrary_evidence: Large insurers can build internal evaluation suites and may be unwilling to expose outputs or incidents.
AI Act applicability varies by use case; a seal cannot substitute for legal compliance or conformity assessment.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: publish a free aggregate Polish claims benchmark, sell one bounded vendor assessment, then convert insurer procurement and release monitoring.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 8 customers in year 2, 30 in year 4, and 80 insurers/vendors across Central Europe in year 6 at 120000 PLN average annual revenue yields 9.6M PLN ARR. At 4-6x ARR and 55-70% founder ownership, founder equity can surpass 5M PLN once 15-20 renewals establish durability.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15-22 hours/week until repeatable evaluation delivery; external insurance/legal reviewers are paid per packet.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 68-80% after expert adjudication, secure environments, and model inference; automation raises margin as the corpus matures.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 6-12 months because enterprise acquisition may cost 20000-40000 PLN, offset by 50000-100000 PLN first-year contracts.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 25000-60000 PLN initial assessment plus 2500-7000 PLN/month continuous testing, with vendor portfolio pricing.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: every model or prompt release triggers regression work; target 90% annual contract renewal if reports are accepted in governance packs.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Evolving Polish claims test corpus, adjudicated failure taxonomy, release-to-incident history, and recognition of a vendor-neutral seal
fingerprint.customer: Polish insurers, claims administrators, and vendors deploying Polish-language AI assistants
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: AI implementation partners, compliance consultancies, procurement templates, and published aggregate benchmark reports
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Domain benchmark, adversarial evaluation report, CI regression API, and time-limited assurance seal
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Insurer or vendor pays per independent assessment and annual continuous-regression license
fingerprint.problem_trigger: AI procurement, production launch, model/vendor change, material prompt change, or control review

founder_fit: Strong match to data science, AI evaluation, adversarial testing, and quantitative scoring.
B2B evidence product avoids influencer-style distribution.
Can begin with synthetic and public policy-language cases without accessing real customer data.
A reusable Polish benchmark can expand from claims communications to adjacent regulated workflows.
risks: False assurance if a model passes a static benchmark but fails in production.
Benchmark leakage and gaming by vendors.
Security and confidentiality requirements could lengthen procurement beyond a part-time founder's capacity.

structure.control_point: procurement-recognized Polish claims benchmark and longitudinal model-release record
structure.critical_dependency: credible expert adjudication and secure access to representative system outputs

thesis: An independent Polish-language regression benchmark for insurance claims copilots and customer communications. Insurers and vendors run each model release against domain-specific factuality, omission, disclosure, fairness, privacy, and escalation tests, creating a longitudinal incident corpus and a procurement-recognized assurance seal.
title: Polish Claims Copilot Benchmark and Seal
uncertainties: Whether insurers prefer vendor-neutral Polish tests to established global assurance firms is unknown.
Access to representative claims communications without personal data must be proven.
The 55000 PLN capital estimate and all commercial figures below are planning hypotheses.
